Valve says the Steam Frame was actually supposed to be cheaper, but then the memory crisis happened and completely messed up those plans

Valve engineers confirmed that they had a specific price target in mind when they designed the VR headset, but the rising cost of RAM and other memory components forced them to increase it.

The Steam Frame is now launching at $1,059 for the 256GB model with VR controllers, while the 1TB version costs $1,299.

Valve engineer Jeremy Selan basically summed up how the team feels about it:

“I wish we could have shipped it at the price that we were at last year.”

Valve could have cut the RAM to save some money, but they decided not to. The Steam Frame has 16GB of LPDDR5X RAM, compared to 8GB in the Quest 3.

The problem is that this makes the price difference pretty brutal. A Quest 3 is around $600, while the Steam Frame starts at over $1,000.

The memory crisis is hitting hardware makers at a really unfortunate time, and Valve clearly isn’t happy about it either.

The Grok @bot team asked me if I had any advice for solopreneurs.

I’ve only been doing this full time for three months, but my advice is to design your business so you can spend more time doing work you actually enjoy.

There will always be choices that could make more money. But if those choices leave you doing work you don’t enjoy, then that defeats the purpose of becoming a solopreneur in the first place.

Delegate that boring work to your bots instead or just don't do it :)

I'm sure most of you know that Half-Life ran on a heavily modified Quake engine. In other words, the most influential shooter of the late 90s stands on code we wrote while id Software was falling to pieces.

I remember some of id Software's people (I won't name names, but not me) mocked Valve for thinking they could even do an awesome game on our software. "Look how long they are taking!" I heard them say. Man alive was THAT opinion wrong. 

I did not share this opinion, because I was a close personal friend of one of Valve's artists (he used to work with me at MicroProse) and had met Gabe Newell personally and he struck me as a stand-up guy. 

Anyway, it's terrific what Valve did. It is exactly what the Quake tech was for, and Valve did stuff with our engine we never would have imagined. 

What I'd like to know, sincerely, when you use someone else's engine, at what point is it no longer their universe, and becomes yours?  

If any of you have shipped on someone else's tech, give me your honest answer.

I just won $12,500.

Not from a job. Not from a raise. From a hackathon.

A kid with a laptop. Late nights. Broken builds. A dream that money could move as fast as the internet.

That dream now has a number on it.

Gemetra just won $12,500 in MNEE at the MNEE Hackathon: Programmable Money for Agents, Commerce, and Automated Finance — out of 1,000+ builders on Devpost.

For years I watched two broken systems steal from ordinary people:

Tourists lose billions in VAT refunds because airport queues, paperwork, and delays kill the claim.

Companies bleed 2–5% fees and wait 3–5 days just to pay their own people.

So I built the thing I wished existed.

Gemetra — wallet-native VAT refunds + global payroll on Ethereum, paid in MNEE. Upload a receipt. Get refunded. Upload a CSV. Pay a team. Instant. Borderless. On-chain.

No bank. No waiting. No “your wire is being processed.”

Just programmable money, doing what money was supposed to do.

This did not fall in my lap.

It was nights after nights. Shipping. Breaking. Shipping again. A demo video. A live app. A public repo. Real MNEE on mainnet — not a mock, not a slide deck.

Hard work still works. Dreams still convert. Rags still turn into a prize check if you refuse to quit.

Thank you to the people who made this real:

@HarbindL   — for product leadership that gave this hackathon a soul. 
@devpost  — 1,000+ of us showed up because you made the arena. 
@MNEE_cash  — thank you for putting $50,000 behind programmable money and then actually awarding it.

I will never forget this.

If you are a builder reading this and thinking “that could never be me” — I was you.

How you win the next MNEE / Devpost hackathon (from someone who just did):
1. Solve a real coordination problem. Judges do not reward “I wrapped a token.” They reward something the world already suffers from. Payroll. Refunds. Treasury. Agents paying agents.

2. Use real MNEE. Contract 0x8ccedbAe4916b79da7F3F612EfB2EB93A2bFD6cF on Ethereum. Meaningful transfers, not a screenshot.

3. Ship a working product. Description + 5-min demo video + live URL + public GitHub with an open-source license. If judges cannot click it, you already lost.

4. Obsess over UX. Beautiful beats clever. A CFO or a tourist should get it in 10 seconds.

5. Show impact. Who uses this tomorrow? How much money moves? How does it scale?

6. Be original. Do not clone Uniswap and slap MNEE on it. Build the thing only you would build.

7. Pick a track and dominate it. AI/Agent Payments. Commerce & Creators. Programmable Finance. Go deep, not wide.

That is the scorecard. That is how $12,500 happens.

If this post reached you — drop a 💚. Share it with one builder who needs to hear it. Tell me what you are building next.
